method: Read-only inspection of four orchestration modules, three regression modules and seven-job workflow. Reopened author local-test log and current files. Test evidence precedes formatting; independently recomputed current SHA/AST, verified against root FORMAT_ONLY before/after record, and checked its before SHA matches the tested source. Original before-format AST values are root-provided attestations, not independently re-derived from unavailable before-format copies. No new Cargo/Bazel or behavior execution.

findings_closed.finding: Stale policy attestation if a later policy read raises.
findings_closed.resolution: verify_tree persists False before reading policy; deletion regression is included.

findings_closed.finding: Toolchain selection string alone did not bind actual Cargo compiler.
findings_closed.resolution: Known inherited rustc/wrapper overrides and Cargo config overrides rejected; exact rustup compiler path SHA/release verified and supplied through RUSTC for subsequent commands.

findings_closed.finding: AWS saved executable copy lacked immediate readback hash.
findings_closed.resolution: Saved copy is now rehashed and must equal original executable SHA before testing; original executable is checked again after execution.

verified_design.artifact_binding: Exact clean source HEAD, typed source allowlist, complete vendor inventory including extra-file rejection, source/Cargo/Bazel snapshots, binary patch, recipe, same run/attempt and producer RESULT SHA. Source and policy checks recur after executing stages.
verified_design.matrix_producer: Independent fixed 6215cb6a87f29623d4beaad24cdf7bcb6bb4fb2c checkout, original Cargo.lock, Matrix SDK/crypto/sqlite exactly0.18.0. Only new driver-provided fixture test patch is applied. Explicit Rust1.95 actual compiler, complete staged-source archive, actual binary and metadata retained.
verified_design.matrix_phase: One actual named test executable. just test exact ignored phase, retries0, no-tests fail. Exactly one fresh JUnit testcase with correct package/classname and no failures/errors/skips/retries. Executable SHA checked before and after.
verified_design.matrix_copy: Complete post-process fixture files including surviving DB/WAL/SHM are hashed; consumer verifies and copies every file before creating writable state. Original bytes rechecked after migration; partial failed after-state is retained. New consumer uses Rust1.96.
verified_design.aws_full_suite: Complete production vendor copied outside main workspace; only frozen standalone lock/nextest config overlaid. Before/after full source inventory.245-case listing includes exactly the original DNS ignore;244 unique JUnit classname/name pairs must equal the complete listing and pass. Both reserved-address timeout assertions remain enabled. Production feature membership is unchanged by qualification overlay.
verified_design.original_deny: deny.toml, original cargo-deny workflow and diagnostics cannot be edited by source patch and remain hash-bound. New workflow invokes the same pinned action against whole codex-rs/Cargo.toml with no added ignore or narrower scan scope.
verified_design.workflow_and_failures: Exact source SHA and same-run named artifacts, hidden files included, normal nonzero failure propagation, no continue-on-error. Matrix step explicitly overrides setup-ci CODEX_REPO_ROOT with baseline. Command logs/exit status and available partial snapshots/JUnit/source/fixture state survive ordinary failures.

limits: Source review and local Python regressions are not remote Rust/Cargo/Bazel/deny qualification.
Compiler checks bind known direct overrides and inspected configs, not a hermetic runner or complete ambient environment.
AWS retains its frozen retry policy and reports passed_after_retry with flaky XML; this is not a first-attempt pass claim. Matrix migration phases reject retries.
Workspace groups rely on actual just/nextest exits and retain produced JUnit; they do not use AWS fixed244 inventory.
Uploads use always() && !cancelled(); externally cancelled runs have no full-preservation guarantee.
Bazel covers listed Linux libraries/consumers, not all-platform or full-workspace behavior. All production policy and authorization gates remain independent.
